A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same softmax-contaminated mixture-of-experts research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and complete Appendices A–B are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 4 and Figures 1–2 report original synthetic-data experiments measuring parameter-estimation errors and empirical convergence rates in distinguishable and non-distinguishable settings.

after.justification: Section 4 and Figures 1–2 retain the original synthetic experiments and their measured estimation errors and fitted convergence rates.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same frozen expert, single Gaussian prompt, softmax gating, and maximum-likelihood estimator implemented through EM with BFGS. The D2 correction concerns a theoretical discrepancy measure, not the fitting objective or algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic Laplace/Gaussian distinguishable setting and two Gaussian non-distinguishable settings involving mean or variance perturbations. Newly cited application domains are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Neither version introduces an empirical baseline comparison. New Table 2 summarizes theoretical comparisons with Yan et al.'s input-free contaminated MoE, already discussed in v1, rather than adding an experimentally evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains eight-dimensional Gaussian covariates, the same ground-truth parameter choices, 20 sample sizes from 10^3 to 10^5, near-truth initialization, and the same estimation-error evaluation. No additional evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The sample-size convergence analysis and two non-distinguishable parameter-perturbation studies are retained. Neither the main text nor the appendices add ablations, robustness tests, or error analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report 40 experiments and display the same error bars in Figures 1–2. There is no added or revised seed information, uncertainty definition, confidence interval, or significance test.

E6.justification: The empirical curves, fitted coefficients, and convergence exponents in Figures 1–2 are unchanged, including the gating-error exponents −0.23 and −0.22 in Figure 2. Table 1 suppresses exp(τ*) factors bounded under the retained compactness assumption, preserving the asymptotic orders; Table 2 supplies an analytical comparison, not new experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces a product of squared distances with their sum in D2's subtraction term, restoring D2(G,G)=0. Theorem 3 also drops v1's explicit strong-identifiability assumption, substantially broadening its stated scope, although Appendix A.3 still invokes that assumption. These changes affect a central mathematical definition and theorem; the remaining proofs are largely unchanged apart from notation and presentation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: distinguishability, near-parametric estimation under separation, slower rates under prompt overlap, and matching minimax lower bounds. The added discussion does not introduce a new headline contribution.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 newly connects the probabilistic model to deterministic deep-learning MoE through the conditional response mean. New Section 3.3 makes design recommendations explicit, largely elaborating v1's existing sample-efficiency and knowledge-overlap interpretations. The single-prompt and Gaussian-prompt limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The synthetic-data formulas, initialization description, EM/BFGS implementation information, and MacBook Air with Apple M4 hardware disclosure are retained. No new code/data access information or additional implementation settings appear.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds sigmoid-gating theory and explicit distinctions concerning uniform rates and minimax bounds. Additional application references are included, while the temperature-efficiency reference is removed. The central positioning relative to input-free contaminated MoE remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds the Challenges discussion and Section 3.3, makes local language and notation edits, updates author affiliations, and moves references before the appendices. Most existing narrative and proof exposition is retained.

P2.justification: The entire document adopts NeurIPS formatting with different typography, margins, spacing, and title layout. Table 2 is added, Table 1's caption is expanded, and the retained Figures 1–2 are resized and placed together on page 10 instead of separate pages. The visual revision extends throughout the appendices.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects D2's failure to vanish at identical parameters and clarifies research positioning and practical implications. However, it removes Theorem 3's strong-identifiability assumption while the unchanged Appendix A.3 proof still explicitly relies on it. This central statement–proof inconsistency offsets a meaningful mathematical correction, and the PDFs do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
